newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Dec 13.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Dec. 13:

WASHINGTON - President Clinton summoned Attorney General Janet Reno to the White House on Thursday night to ask her to stay in his second term, and he appeared close to naming a pair of political allies to two other Cabinet posts.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton reacted sceptically to the D.C. federal control board's request that the federal government take over about $1 billion worth of District government programmes that typically are paid for by states.
WASHINGTON - Retailers are aglow over the pace of holiday sales. With the economy and spirits up, consumers are spending.

VERMILION CLIFFS, Ariz. - After an absence of nearly a century, California condors flew again over the red sandstone cliffs, riding updrafts that conservationists hope hope will carry the rare birds back from the abyss of extinction.
WASHINGTON - Maryland commuters using Interstate 270 will find one lane restricted to car pools during rush hour starting next week.
WASHINGTON - A sharp drop in violent crime among the youngest offenders, those under the age of 15, was the driving force behind an unexpected decline in juvenile crime last year.

WASHINGTON - Startling new research indicates that the evolutionary predecessor of present-day humans -- a smaller-brained, thicker-boned, heavy duty species called Homo erectus -- may have lived alongside anatomically modern people for tens of thousands of years in Asia.
